issues.description: Element: SealSaloon.stock (the stock attribute). The problem statement first instructs that the SealSaloon stock should be initialized in the SealSaloon constructor (problem_statement.md lines 70-71), but elsewhere in the same problem statement it explicitly requires that the stock attribute must be static (shared across instances) (problem_statement.md lines 77-80). The reference solution declares stock as a static field and initializes it at declaration (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java lines 4-6). These two instructions conflict: initializing a static field in an instance constructor is misleading and leaves students uncertain whether stock must be an instance field initialized in the constructor or a static field initialized at declaration or in a static initializer.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the problem statement so it is not contradictory. If stock must be shared across all saloon instances, state that SealSaloon.stock is static and show that students should declare and (optionally) initialize it at declaration or in a static initializer. Remove or reword the sentence that requires initializing stock in the instance constructor. Example: "Declare a static final Stock stock (shared across all SealSaloon instances). You may initialize it at the point of declaration or in a static initializer; the instance constructor should not be used to initialize this static field."

issues.description: Element: SealSaloon.totalOrders. The UML in the problem statement shows totalOrders as an int (problem_statement.md lines 27-29: "-totalOrders: int"), but the reference solution declares totalOrders as a long (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java line 6: "private long totalOrders = 0;"). This mismatch in the primitive type for the same conceptual attribute may confuse students about which type to use and what the getter's return type should be.
issues.suggestedFix: Pick one primitive type for totalOrders and make the problem statement, UML, and examples consistent. Either change the UML and textual description to use "long" or update the reference solution to use "int". Document the chosen type explicitly (e.g., "Use an int totalOrders to track the number of orders") so students know which type and getter return type to implement.
